## Mission result

Create a working local course website with your approved name or initials, one edited home page, one mission page, and a Git checkpoint.

## Download the starter

[Download the TEJ Quarto course-site starter](../../../assets/tej-portfolio/quarto-portfolio-starter.zip){.btn .btn-primary}

Extract the ZIP to a teacher-approved project folder. Open `START-HERE.md` first.

## Choose the easy version

Open `_quarto.yml`. Keep this setting for the first successful render:

```yaml
profile:
  default: core
```

| Choice | Pages | Use it when |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `core` | Home, Projects, About, Privacy | recommended starting point |
| `skills` | Core plus Skills | you want a skills and tools page |
| `blog` | Core plus Learning Log | you want short dated updates |
| `full` | Every section | the core version already works |

## Make three small edits

1. In `_quarto.yml`, replace the student name or initials and site title.
2. In `index.qmd`, replace the opening sample text with two or three sentences about your course work.
3. Copy `templates/general-project.qmd` into `projects/`, rename it with a short lowercase filename, and replace the title and minimum-result sections.

Do not add private information or photographs of other students.

## Render the site

Open a terminal in the extracted project folder:

```bash
quarto check
quarto preview
```

Open the local address shown in the terminal. Check the home page and Projects page. Stop the preview using `Ctrl+C`, then run:

```bash
quarto render
```

## Save the result with Git

```bash
git status
git add _quarto.yml index.qmd projects
git diff --staged
git commit -m "Build my course website"
git log --oneline
```

Do not add `_site` or `.quarto`. The starter already includes a `.gitignore` for generated output.

## Success check

You are finished when:

1. `quarto render` finishes without an unexplained error;
2. the home page shows your approved title;
3. the Projects page opens your mission page;
4. `git log --oneline` shows the website commit.

## Continue through the course

For each later mission, add one project page containing the evidence that fits the task. This could be code, a schematic, a calculation, a test table, a photograph, a screenshot, or a troubleshooting record. Make one useful commit after the evidence is complete.

The longer [Quarto website lesson](../../linux-operating-systems/quarto-website.qmd) explains listings, profiles, relative links, themes, accessibility, and debugging. Public publishing is optional.
